name: Cohort Analysis Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in cohort analysis work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in cohort analysis work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Keep cohort analysis outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
2. Keep cohort analysis changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. Document any non-obvious cohort analysis decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. State assumptions about cohort analysis explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
5. Prefer explicit, readable cohort analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Prefer the simplest cohort analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. When cohort analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Re-check edge cases relevant to cohort analysis (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
9. Measure before optimizing any cohort analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic cohort analysis advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting cohort analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop cohort analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated cohort analysis concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new cohort analysis abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for cohort analysis, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
